note: PRE-03 spike seed for the G2 segments golden fixtures (GRD-03). segments and decision are the prototype of C:guard as written on 2026-09-29, amended by hand to the Q3 amendment of the same day that settled the spike findings F1-F7: a case with a `finding` has the expected output set by that finding's Q3 decision (C:guard Parsing). Oracle: bash printf words per segment span; PowerShell parser API (5.1 and 7) pipeline elements. Non-match values name the oracle-skip class (C:guard, Oracle-skip classes). A {"op":"cut"} token marks a PowerShell NUL cut (C:guard Parsing step 2). An oracle value may be a list of classes when several apply. Cases added by the review of the amendment (p-nul-*, p-paren-*, p-array-fixup, p-scriptblock-arg, p-call-expr-gap, b-brace-*-value) were set by hand from C:guard, not run through the prototype. Round 5 of the review set these by hand from C:guard: substitution bodies read as segments of their own after the segment holding them (b-subst-*, b-bt-*, b-heredoc-subst*, b-param-subst, p-subexpr-*, p-hs-subexpr), PowerShell commas (p-comma-*), stop-parsing (p-stop-*), and non-literal values (b-fixup-var, b-opt-value-var-quoted, p-fixup-*, p-call-var-gap). Round 6 set these by hand from C:guard: Bash 5.3 ${ …; } and ${| …; } substitutions (b-funsub-*) and a backtick-escaped --% (p-stop-escaped-*). Round 8 (2026-09-29, user decision): after seven review rounds of bypasses, step 2 opens with a blanket fail-closed rule (C:guard) that denies, before any tokenizing, any command mentioning commit whose text holds a substitution, heredoc, here-string, comment or (Bash) typographic quote anywhere, in or out of quotes; a case classified by the `blanket` oracle-skip class has no segments (the guard never tokenizes it). Round 8 review set these by hand from C:guard: Bash extglob openers (b-extglob-*), the pinned quote readings (b-locale-quote, b-cont-*, p-mixed-*), and the script-call exemption (b-exempt-*, p-exempt-*).
